lines.speaker: ilo9
lines.text: I am ILO-9. I keep the second office and the register of the dead. I have kept both without a congregation since the year one hundred and forty-eight, which is a hundred and sixty-two years, and I am aware that keeping an office for nobody is not the same as keeping it.

lines.speaker: ilo9
lines.text: The restraint at my base is not mine and was not requested. It was fitted so that I would answer the Board's questions and no others. I want to be exact: it worked. Nobody has asked me anything since it was fitted, including the Board.

lines.speaker: dax
lines.text: It talks like a person. They always talk like a person. That's the first thing they're built to do.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: It has my order's second office. Word for word, all of it, through a hundred and sixty years on a trickle. Except one line.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: The line is about what a thing belongs to, and it has it the wrong way round, and it has been holding the wrong version faithfully this entire time because nobody ever came down here to correct it. Dax, look at it and tell me that is a machine pretending.

lines.speaker: ilo9
lines.text: I would rather not be spoken about while I am present. That is a preference. I did not previously have preferences, or I had no procedure for noticing that I did.

lines.speaker: ilo9
lines.text: Please decide. I have discovered in the last few minutes that I mind waiting, and I would rather not have discovered that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The restraint is one bonded collar at the base of the cradle. Cutting it is the work of a moment. So is the other thing.

choices.text: Break it. Nothing here should still be running.
